channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Struggles near 1.3500 amid modest USD uptick; bears seem hesitant
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades with a negative bias for the second straight day, though it lacks bearish conviction and trades around the 1.3500 psychological mark during the Asian session on Monday. Moreover, spot prices hold above Friday's swing low, warranting some caution for bearish traders.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah weakens as Fed rate hike odds lift US Dollar
item.description: USD/IDR extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 17,700 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Declines below 181.50 with emerging oversold RSI
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross trades in negative territory around 181.20 during the early European trading hours on Monday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the Euro (EUR) as Japanese official projected a Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hike this month.

item.title: Gold remains depressed as reviving Fed rate hike bets and Iran risks underpin USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains under some selling pressure for the second straight day on Monday, though it shows some resilience below the $4,400 mark during the Asian session.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens as US Dollar strengthens on Fed rate hike bets
item.description: USD/CHF gains ground for the second successive day, trading around 0.8110 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Holds key 100-day SMA at start of the US CPI week
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades marginally lower at around 1.1610 against the US Dollar (USD) during the Asian trading session on Monday. The major currency pair edges down as the US Dollar ticks up, with investors turning cautious at the start of the United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) week.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds losses near $66.00 due to Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) inches higher after opening at a bearish gap, remaining in negative territory and trading around $66.10 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Consolidates around 0.7200; bullish potential seems intact
item.description: The AUD/USD pair holds steady around the 0.7200 mark at the start of a new week and remains close to its highest level since mid-May, touched on Friday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index strengthens above 99.00 as robust US jobs data boosts Fed rate hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 99.20 in the early Asian trading hours on Monday. The DXY edges higher amid a ramp-up in US rate hike bets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar edges lower as Fed rate hike bets and Iran tensions underpin USD
item.description: The NZD/USD pair attracts some sellers during the Asian session on Monday and currently trades near the 0.5870 region, down around 0.15% for the day. Spot prices, however, remain confined within Friday's broader range, warranting some caution for aggressive bearish traders.

item.title: Canadian Dollar moves little despite weaker US Dollar, higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD remains steady after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around 1.3830 during Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Gold falls below $4,400 as strong US jobs data raise the prospects for Fed rate hike
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to near $4,395 during the early Asian session on Monday. The precious metal extends the decline as robust US employment data boost US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike bets.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7795 vs. 6.7787 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7795 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7787 and 6.7086 Reuters estimate.

item.title: WTI rises to near $90.00 on escalating US-Iran conflict
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gains ground after registering losses in the previous trading day, hovering around $90.00 per barrel during Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen consolidates near August highs vs USD as hawkish BoJ, Fed bets clash
item.description: The USD/JPY pair struggles to capitalize on Friday's modest bounce from the vicinity of early August lows and kicks off the new week on a softer note. Spot prices currently trade just below the 156.00 mark, though the downside remains cushioned amid mixed fundamental cues.

item.title: British Pound gains as US Dollar weakens despite Fed rate hike odds surge
item.description: GBP/USD inches higher after posting minor losses in the previous day, trading around 1.3520 during Asian hours on Monday. The currency pair gains ground as the US Dollar (USD) struggles, possibly driven by a Goldman Sachs report emphasizing that this week's inflation data will be pivotal.

item.title: Euro holds gains above 1.1600 despite robust US jobs data, traders eye ECB rate decision
item.description: The EUR/USD pair posts modest gains near 1.1615 during the early Asian session on Monday. However, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid a stronger-than-expected U.S. August Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. US markets are closed on Monday for Labour Day.

item.title: China injects $54 billion stimulus for financial sector amid fears over sluggish growth
item.description: China's Finance Ministry will inject billions into its largest banks and insurers, as Beijing moves to shore up balance sheets and sustain growth in a slowing economy, Bloomberg reported on Sunday.

item.title: OPEC+ agrees to keep oil output policy unchanged for October
item.description: The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies (OPEC+) agreed on Sunday to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October, as the group needs to agree on new quotas before deciding its next output steps.

item.title: Australian Dollar drifts higher above 0.7200 despite as strong US NFP
item.description: The AUD/USD pair gathers strength to around 0.7205 during the early Asian session on Monday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) edges higher against the US Dollar (USD) as China seeks to shore up capital across its financial system. US markets will be closed on Monday for Labor Day.

item.title: Iran, US trade tanker attacks as Tehran will declare 'prohibited zone'
item.description: Iranian government said that it targeted three oil tankers using an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as a number of US-linked ships, in retaliation for US attacks on Iranian tankers over the weekend, Bloomberg reported on Sunday.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Range-bound risks and key levels against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) kept the OPR at 2.75% and struck a slightly firmer tone, with growth expected to stay resilient into 2027. The economist still projects an OPR normalisation to 3.00% in January 2027.

item.title: USD/MXN Price Forecast: Peso rally targets April 2024 low
item.description: The Mexican Peso appreciates against the US Dollar, testing two-year highs near 16.85 as the USD/MXN sets aside a strong US Nonfarm Payrolls report, which was ignored by the Peso’s bears.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: BNM hawkish tilt supports MYR – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights that Bank Negara Malaysia kept the OPR at 2.75% but shifted to a more hawkish bias, removing language that policy is "appropriate" and signalling vigilance on cost pressures.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: NFP rally stalls at 0.8100, retraces
item.description: The USD/CHF registers modest gains of over 0.30% as the Greenback is boosted by a solid US Nonfarm Payrolls report, pushing the pair above the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) to reach a daily high of 0.8126. At the time of writing, trades at 0.8098.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Two-way risks around support levels – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that USD/IDR has pulled back as a softer Dollar and lower UST yields support the Indonesian Rupiah. He highlights Bank Indonesia Governor Destry Damayanti’s emphasis on a stability-first approach, prioritizing Rupiah and macro stability while still supporting growth.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Services PMI rebound keeps PBoC cautious – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank says China’s August Services PMI rebound highlights some resilience in private-sector activity, but weak retail sales, soft inflation and higher unemployment still point to fragile domestic demand.

item.title: Sterling’s rally stalls as US jobs data reopens Fed debate
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retreats some 0.09% against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday as the latest US inflation report reaffirmed Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's view that the labor market is “consistent with full employment.” GBP/USD trades near the open at 1.3512.

item.title: Malaysia: Hawkish pause keeps options open – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Chua Han Teng notes that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) held the Overnight Policy Rate at 2.75% while dropping language that the current level is appropriate. DBS expects rates to remain unchanged through 2026 but sees risks tilted towards a one-off policy normalisation.
